main.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2
main.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 is a 2009 first-person shooter game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision.

cards.heading: Modern Warfare continues
cards.text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 is a 2009 first-person shooter game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision. It is the sixth installment in the Call of Duty series and the direct sequel to Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare. It was released worldwide on November 10, 2009, for Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360. A separate version for the Nintendo DS, titled Modern Warfare: Mobilized, was also released on the same day. A version for OS X was developed by Aspyr and released in May 2014, and the Xbox 360 version was made backward compatible for the Xbox One in 2018.

cards.heading: Task Force 141 and the Army Rangers
cards.text: The game's campaign follows Task Force 141, a multinational special forces unit commanded by Captain Soap MacTavish as they hunt Vladimir Makarov, leader of the Russian Ultranationalist party, and United States Army Rangers from the 1st Ranger Battalion who are defending the Washington, D.C. area from a Russian invasion. The game's main playable characters are Sergeant Gary "Roach" Sanderson, of the 141, and Private James Ramirez, of the Army Rangers, with Captain MacTavish becoming playable later in the campaign. The multiplayer mode was expanded upon from the previous game, with several new features and modes.

cards.heading: Development and map packs
cards.text: Development for the game began in 2008, when it was still known as Call of Duty 6. It uses the IW 4.0 engine, an improved version of Call of Duty 4's IW 3.0. Infinity Ward was inspired by real-life conflicts when developing the campaign mode. They initially tested the multiplayer mode by playing an in-house beta version of the game. Modern Warfare 2 was officially announced in February 2009. Teasing of the game began in March, with short trailers being released for the game and, eventually, a full reveal trailer. The multiplayer mode was revealed shortly after. Two downloadable content packs were released for it post-release, each containing five new multiplayer maps, with some being remastered maps from Call of Duty 4.

cards.heading: Reception and the airport controversy
cards.text: Modern Warfare 2 sold approximately 4.7 million copies in North America and the United Kingdom during its first day, becoming the United States' best-selling game of 2009. Reviewers praised its campaign, multiplayer and amount of content, while questioning the short campaign and limited innovation. Its airport terrorist-attack mission also provoked controversy about the actions it asked players to perform. Modern Warfare 3 concluded the original storyline in 2011. A campaign-only remaster returned in 2020, revisiting the single-player story separately from the multiplayer that accompanied it.

main.title: New Super Mario Bros. Wii
main.summary: New Super Mario Bros. Wii makes a side-scrolling Mario adventure a shared activity. Up to four players cooperate or compete across the same stages, with a Super Guide available when progress stalls.

cards.heading: Four players enter the Mushroom Kingdom
cards.text: New Super Mario Bros. Wii is a 2009 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii. A follow-up to New Super Mario Bros., it was first released in Australia, North America, and Europe in November 2009, followed by Japan a month later. It was released on the Wii U's Virtual Console in 2016, though only in Europe, Australia and Japan. A port in high definition resolution for the Nvidia Shield TV was released only in China in December 2017. Like other side-scrolling Super Mario games, the player controls Mario as he travels eight worlds and fights Bowser's army to save Princess Peach. New Super Mario Bros. Wii was the first Super Mario game to feature simultaneous cooperative multiplayer gameplay; up to four people can play in cooperative and competitive multiplayer modes, taking control of Mario as well as Luigi and two Toads, Yellow Toad and Blue Toad. The game also introduced "Super Guide", which allows the player to watch a computer-controlled character complete a level.

cards.heading: Cooperation, challenge and Super Guide
cards.text: Miyamoto wanted cooperative Mario play to accommodate both skilled players and beginners. The Wii follow-up therefore combined a stronger challenge with ways to step aside from it. A player could enter a floating bubble and let companions carry the action forward, while Super Guide offered help through difficult sections. Avoiding that assistance supplied another goal for experienced players. The design makes sharing a level part of its difficulty: one person can keep moving while another recovers. Shiho Fujii and Ryo Nagamatsu composed the music, with Koji Kondo advising on sound.

cards.heading: Reception and sales
cards.text: The game was announced following a slight drop in profits, with Nintendo hoping its release would help to rejuvenate sales of the Wii. New Super Mario Bros. Wii was both critically and commercially successful, receiving particular praise for the introduction of its multiplayer aspect, while its gameplay and level design were also praised, although some critics were disappointed by its lack of innovation compared to its predecessor and previous Super Mario titles. It received several honors, including the Best Wii Game award from the 2009 Spike Video Game Awards, IGN, and GameTrailers, and is the fourth-best-selling game for the Wii as of March 2021, having sold 30.32 million copies worldwide. In 2012, it was followed by New Super Mario Bros. 2 for the Nintendo 3DS and New Super Mario Bros. U for the Wii U.

main.title: Assassin's Creed II
main.subtitle: Learning the Renaissance by Running Across Its Roofs
main.summary: Ezio Auditore crosses Renaissance Italy through climbing routes, viewpoints and inventions supplied by Leonardo da Vinci.

cards.heading: Ezio in Renaissance Italy
cards.text: Assassin's Creed II turns Florence, Venice, San Gimignano and other Renaissance locations into places to explore as Ezio Auditore. Towers, palaces, squares and rooftops supply routes and escape opportunities. Ubisoft combines historical settings with fiction, placing Ezio alongside figures such as Leonardo da Vinci.

cards.heading: Routes across Florence
cards.text: Ledges, beams, roofs and towers create routes across Florence. Recognisable monuments become landmarks that Ezio can reach and climb. The city's proportions are adapted to his movement, connecting its architecture to the choices a player makes when travelling or escaping pursuit.

cards.heading: Climbing the viewpoints
cards.text: Climbing a viewpoint reveals the skyline and synchronises part of the map. A prominent building becomes both a destination and a way to understand the surrounding city. The expanded view gives the player information for planning the next journey through its streets and roofs.

cards.heading: Leonardo's inventions
cards.text: Leonardo repairs the hidden blade, deciphers pages and supplies inventions for Ezio to use. His flying machine becomes a playable sequence, joining the fictional adventure to a historical figure's interest in invention. The relationship gives the player practical reasons to return to Leonardo as new tools become available.

main.title: Left 4 Dead 2
main.summary: Left 4 Dead 2 is a 2009 first-person shooter game by Valve.

cards.heading: Four new Survivors
cards.text: Left 4 Dead 2 is a 2009 first-person shooter game by Valve. The sequel to Left 4 Dead (2008) and the second game in the Left 4 Dead series, it was released for Windows and Xbox 360 in November 2009, Mac OS X in October 2010, and Linux in July 2013.

cards.heading: The Director and new infected
cards.text: Left 4 Dead 2 builds upon cooperatively focused gameplay and Valve's proprietary Source engine, the same game engine used in the original Left 4 Dead. Set during the aftermath of an apocalyptic pandemic, the game focuses on four new Survivors, fighting against hordes of zombies known as the Infected, who develop severe psychosis and act extremely aggressive. The Survivors must fight their way through five campaigns, interspersed with safe houses that act as checkpoints, with the goal of escape at each campaign's finale. The gameplay is procedurally altered by the "AI Director 2.0", which monitors the players' performance and adjusts the scenario to provide a dynamic challenge. Other new features include new types of Special Infected and an arsenal of melee weapons.

cards.heading: Reception and regional restrictions
cards.text: The game made its world premiere at E3 2009 with a trailer during the Microsoft press event. Prior to release, it received mixed critical and community reactions, and attracted an unusually high volume of controversy about its graphic content. In response, alterations were made to the cover art, but both Australia and Germany refused to rate the unmodified edition at the time of release (both have since been reclassified to R18+ and 18, respectively). Despite this, the game was met with positive critical reviews, and is considered to be one of the greatest video games ever made and one of the best multiplayer games.

main.title: Professor Layton and the Last Specter
main.subtitle: Before Luke became an apprentice
main.summary: Professor Layton and the Last Specter is Level-5's Nintendo DS prequel showing how Layton first met Luke. Joined by assistant Emmy Altava, he investigates the village of Misthallery and the mystery surrounding its apparent specter. Released as The Spectre's Call in Europe, it moves the series back before the original trilogy. That change lets the familiar partnership begin again as a question rather than an established fact. The player explores illustrated streets, talks to residents and solves the puzzles that stand between a rumour and its explanation.

cards.heading: Before Luke became an apprentice
cards.text: Professor Layton and the Last Specter is Level-5's Nintendo DS prequel showing how Layton first met Luke. Joined by assistant Emmy Altava, he investigates the village of Misthallery and the mystery surrounding its apparent specter. Released as The Spectre's Call in Europe, it moves the series back before the original trilogy. That change lets the familiar partnership begin again as a question rather than an established fact. The player explores illustrated streets, talks to residents and solves the puzzles that stand between a rumour and its explanation.

cards.heading: Search the village with a tap
cards.text: Touching the scenery can reveal dialogue, hint coins, collectibles or hidden puzzles, while a visible resident can be selected for a conversation. The village opens gradually as the investigation progresses. Puzzles that become inaccessible can be recovered later by Keats the Cat, preserving an opportunity to solve them. The system encourages attention without requiring every discovery to happen at the first possible moment. Misthallery becomes a place that can be searched patiently, with the same image offering another reason to look after its first conversation has ended.

cards.heading: A larger life around the mystery
cards.text: Some editions also include Professor Layton's London Life, a separate role-playing diversion set in Little London with characters from the series. It was omitted from the European release, an important difference beneath the regional title change. The main investigation keeps the series' varied brainteasers and measured pace, while the prequel gives Luke's behaviour another significance. The audience already knows who he will become. Watching the relationship form allows an ordinary exchange or successful deduction to carry part of that future companionship before the characters themselves recognise it.

main.title: Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes
main.subtitle: An army arranged like a puzzle
main.summary: Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes is Capybara Games' Nintendo DS role-playing adventure built around tactical battles between grids of soldiers. Heroes from different factions explore the world of Ashan, recruit forces and pursue connected stories, with each confrontation asking the player to arrange units into useful formations. Matching pieces prepares attacks that will travel toward the opposing side after a delay. The army is therefore both a collection of characters and a puzzle surface, where moving one soldier can help prepare a larger action several turns before it actually happens.

cards.heading: An army arranged like a puzzle
cards.text: Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes is Capybara Games' Nintendo DS role-playing adventure built around tactical battles between grids of soldiers. Heroes from different factions explore the world of Ashan, recruit forces and pursue connected stories, with each confrontation asking the player to arrange units into useful formations. Matching pieces prepares attacks that will travel toward the opposing side after a delay. The army is therefore both a collection of characters and a puzzle surface, where moving one soldier can help prepare a larger action several turns before it actually happens.

cards.heading: An attack needs time to charge
cards.text: A turn provides a limited number of moves for shifting units and forming groups of the same colour. A completed vertical formation begins charging, announcing an attack that the opponent can try to interrupt before it launches. Its path then interacts with the units standing between it and the enemy hero. The waiting period makes prediction important. Preparing a powerful action can create pressure, but the formation must survive long enough to deliver it, giving the opponent a visible problem and a chance to respond before the damage arrives.

cards.heading: Different factions change the arrangement
cards.text: Each faction supplies basic troops alongside larger advanced units, and the available selection shapes how its army can be assembled. Heroes gain experience and abilities through exploration and battles, while equipment can modify what the army or its leader can do. Multiplayer provides another setting in which to test those arrangements against a human opponent. The puzzle rules remain readable across the different forces, allowing the wider adventure to introduce new capabilities without abandoning the central question of which formation should be prepared now and whether it can remain intact until its turn arrives.

main.title: Phantasy Star Portable 2
main.subtitle: A new mercenary joins Little Wing
main.summary: Phantasy Star Portable 2 is Alfa System's PSP action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 3 December 2009. The player creates a character who joins Little Wing, a private mercenary group based on the Clad 6 resort colony. Set three years after the earlier Portable adventure, the story follows a society facing depleted resources and plans for migration. Missions provide the immediate work of the mercenary career, while the character's appearance and development make the resulting adventurer personal. The series' science-fiction equipment and fantasy combat continue within a structure suited to portable play.

cards.heading: A new mercenary joins Little Wing
cards.text: Phantasy Star Portable 2 is Alfa System's PSP action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 3 December 2009. The player creates a character who joins Little Wing, a private mercenary group based on the Clad 6 resort colony. Set three years after the earlier Portable adventure, the story follows a society facing depleted resources and plans for migration. Missions provide the immediate work of the mercenary career, while the character's appearance and development make the resulting adventurer personal. The series' science-fiction equipment and fantasy combat continue within a structure suited to portable play.

cards.heading: The energy belongs to the character
cards.text: Photon Points are attached to the character rather than individual weapons, changing how the resource is managed across available equipment. Guarding, evasive movement and offensive abilities give the player several ways to respond during real-time encounters. Character creation includes appearance and voice choices before that combat career begins. Equipment and development remain reasons to repeat missions, as a successful expedition can improve the options brought to the next one. The connection between the created character and the available fighting tools becomes the continuity running through the changing assignments and enemies.

cards.heading: A portable adventure keeps room for a party
cards.text: Single-player missions coexist with multiplayer, allowing the same broad action role-playing structure to become a shared expedition. Yuya Kimura directed the game, with a score including Hideaki Kobayashi, Fumie Kumatani and Kenichi Tokoi. International editions followed in September 2010. The sequel develops the earlier Portable format through its revised resource system and expanded action choices while retaining the appeal of a customised adventurer gathering equipment with others. Its place in Phantasy Star's history comes from carrying that cooperative mission-and-growth rhythm onto PSP without reducing the player's character to a fixed hero.

main.title: The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks
main.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks is a 2009 action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo DS handheld game console and the direct sequel to the 2007 Nintendo DS game Phantom Hourglass.

cards.heading: A train journey across New Hyrule
cards.text: The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks is a 2009 action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo DS handheld game console and the direct sequel to the 2007 Nintendo DS game Phantom Hourglass. Set a century after the events of Phantom Hourglass, the storyline follows a new Link and the great-great-granddaughter of Tetra, Princess Zelda, as they explore the land of New Hyrule to prevent the awakening of the Demon King Malladus. Players navigate New Hyrule, completing quests that advance the story and solving environmental and dungeon-based puzzles, many requiring use of the DS's touchscreen and other hardware features. Navigation between towns and dungeons is done using a train, which features its own set of mechanics and puzzles.

cards.heading: Building a sequel with a more active Zelda
cards.text: Production began in 2007 following the release of Phantom Hourglass, with half the team including director Daiki Iwamoto and producer Eiji Aonuma returning. Aonuma got the concept from a children's book and incorporated some of its elements into the game. Originally planned as a quickly produced sequel similar to Majora's Mask, production took two years because of the new features. The character of Zelda was given more agency and a key role in both the narrative and several puzzles, breaking away from her earlier passive characterisations. The game was lauded by critics from both dedicated video game outlets and general journalistic sites. Praise was directed towards its narrative and gameplay concepts.

main.title: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors
main.subtitle: Nine strangers inside a sinking ship
main.summary: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors is Chunsoft's Nintendo DS visual novel and escape-room adventure, the first game in the Zero Escape series. College student Junpei wakes aboard a sinking liner with eight other abducted people. They are forced into the Nonary Game, where numbered doors and strict rules determine how they can proceed. The immediate task is to escape, but the group also has to decide whom to trust. A closed room becomes one problem inside a larger uncertainty about the people sharing it.

cards.heading: Nine strangers inside a sinking ship
cards.text: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors is Chunsoft's Nintendo DS visual novel and escape-room adventure, the first game in the Zero Escape series. College student Junpei wakes aboard a sinking liner with eight other abducted people. They are forced into the Nonary Game, where numbered doors and strict rules determine how they can proceed. The immediate task is to escape, but the group also has to decide whom to trust. A closed room becomes one problem inside a larger uncertainty about the people sharing it.

cards.heading: Read the room, then choose the door
cards.text: The adventure alternates between narrative passages and Escape sections. In a room, the player examines objects, collects items and works through connected puzzles to find a way onward. Between those practical problems, conversations and decisions shape the route through the ship. The change of pace makes investigation operate on two levels. An object may have a definite use once it is understood, while a person's explanation can remain doubtful. Solving the lock does not settle whether the next decision will place the group in greater danger.

cards.heading: Another ending changes the question
cards.text: The story branches toward several endings, making the route taken through the ship part of what the player understands about its mystery. Knowledge from an earlier attempt can change how a familiar conversation is read, even before another door has opened. Kotaro Uchikoshi connects the puzzle structure to that accumulating uncertainty rather than treating the rooms as detachable diversions. The handheld's two screens support a game built around reading and acting, giving the same small machine room for an urgent narrative and the close inspection of an apparently ordinary object.

main.title: Angry Birds
main.subtitle: A small gesture brings down a world
main.summary: On December 11, 2009, Rovio released Angry Birds on iPhone.

cards.heading: Rovio's fifty-second game
cards.text: Rovio released Angry Birds for iPhone on December 11, 2009. The Finnish studio's fifty-second game combines a touch-controlled slingshot with structures built from wood, glass and stone. Pulling back and releasing launches a bird into the scene, where impacts can bring down a tower. Quick restarts make it easy to try a different angle.

cards.heading: Aiming with a fingertip
cards.text: The finger pulls the bird directly away from the slingshot. Distance and direction set the launch, connecting the touch gesture to the resulting arc. Watching the first impact helps the player adjust the next attempt, with small differences sometimes producing a very different collapse.

cards.heading: Materials and collapsing structures
cards.text: Wood, glass and stone react differently to a hit. A shot can remove a support and start a chain reaction that reaches targets beyond the bird's direct path. Additional birds introduce different abilities within the same setup, giving players more ways to approach each structure.

cards.heading: From the App Store to a wider audience
cards.text: Rovio developed Angry Birds over roughly eight months after years of work on other mobile games. The studio was under financial pressure when it launched. Downloads and updates gradually expanded the audience, followed by toys, animation and films. Short, repeatable levels remained the basis of a game that was easy to show to someone else.
